bible:
# PLAN, NO PLAN: series bible

## 1. Premise

Two best friends travel to football matches abroad. Timo plans every minute. Luna plans nothing. Each film is one small trip problem where his way meets her way. One of them says "No", and one cut later they are both doing it and laughing.

Each film is one complete small story of 22 to 30 seconds. Someone who watches one film, once, with the sound off, can say what happened in one sentence.

## 2. Tone

- Sunny, quick, warm and a little cheeky. The two tease each other with some bite and always end closer.
- Friends, never a couple. They push each other, laugh at each other, hang an arm on a shoulder. The big hug of each film goes to the object (the suitcase, the backpack, the food), not to each other. No hand-holding, no long looks.
- Each is right in turn. Her way wins one film, his plan wins the next. Nobody is the fool and nobody is taught a lesson.
- Real fans. They are loud and a bit wild when it matters. Food and coffee, never beer as the joke.
- The town is generous, and the locals they meet are mostly their own age. Making a friend at an away match is part of the dream.
- Voices are natural and low-key: light second-language accents, contractions ("It's one night"), laughs that are not cut clean. Never bright cartoon acting.
- It never feels like a brand: no header line, no slogan, no narrator, no "hey guys".

## 3. The rules that keep every film clear

1. **One sentence first.** Every film starts from its retell sentence: who wants what, what gets in the way, how it pays off. If the sentence cannot be said in one breath, the film is not made.
2. **Two people, known in two seconds.** Tall, teal, big watch, tiny backpack is Plan. Short, coral, hands full is No Plan. No name and no word is needed to tell them apart.
3. **The problem is in frame one.** The first frame shows both friends and the one big object of the film, already in conflict (a tiny backpack beside a giant suitcase). No establishing shot, no title.
4. **One object carries the film.** It is the biggest, brightest thing in frame one (the suitcase, the flatbread, the poncho, the scarf rail). First it is the problem, then it is the answer. A viewer who watches only that object can follow the story.
5. **The watch is the clock.** Timo's big yellow watch shows time pressure with no number: a finger on the watch means hurry, hands on the head mean late, a look at it and a smile mean they made it.
6. **One idea per shot.** A shot is held at least 3 seconds and at most two things happen in it. If a shot needs a third "then", it is split or it starts later.
7. **Cause you can see, in order.** Slow uphill, fast downhill. The answer comes out of the problem object in front of the camera; we never cut to a result with no visible link.
8. **Only the story is on screen.** A film has the two friends, at most one local, and the cat for one shot. A local gets a clear first moment alone in the frame before doing anything. Nobody appears unexplained in the background.
9. **Every sound that matters has a picture.** A roar is also bunting shaking or arms going up. Drums are also a drummer or a stream of scarves moving one way. Nothing important is only heard.
10. **Words are a bonus.** At most one short spoken line per shot (3 to 5 words, never more than 10) that names what the picture already shows. Every film is cut and approved silent first.
11. **One text at a time.** The only text is the caption of the line being spoken. No header, no second line, and no sign, screen, letter or number inside the picture.
12. **The last frame answers the first.** Same framing, opposite feeling (shock at the suitcase, then a hug for the suitcase). The payoff is an action on a face. It is never a caption, a sound or the end card.
13. **Each film stands alone.** No recap, no joke that needs an earlier film, no cliffhanger.
14. **Two gates before release.** (a) The start pictures of all shots, laid side by side like a comic strip with no text, must tell the story. (b) The finished film is shown once, muted, on a phone, to a young viewer and to an adult with English as a second language, who have seen nothing. It is released only if their one sentence matches ours.

## 4. Cast

### Timo, 23: "Plan"
Very tall and thin (about 190 cm), long legs and arms, stands very straight. Dark brown skin, long oval face, high cheekbones, big round dark-brown eyes, thick straight eyebrows that tilt up in the middle when he worries, a wide mouth with a shy smile, clean-shaven. Black tight curls in a short neat flat-top with sharp edges. No glasses.
Always wears: a deep teal retro track jacket, zipped up, collar standing, one cream stripe down each sleeve; straight dark navy trousers that end above the ankle; cream socks; clean white trainers; a small square teal backpack high on both shoulders; a huge chunky sunflower-yellow watch with a blank face, worn over the jacket cuff so it always shows. Trip scarf knotted once at the throat, both ends the same length.
Who he is: he has planned every minute and loves being early. He is the bigger football fan of the two and missing kick-off is his only real fear. He moves in straight lines, quick and exact. When the plan breaks he freezes for one beat with his eyebrows up, says no, and then enjoys it more than anyone. Gentle, never bossy, first to laugh at himself.
Voice (locked): soft, quick, light tenor, light non-native accent.

### Luna, 22: "No Plan"
Short and sturdy (about 158 cm, she reaches his shoulder), strong legs, weight on one hip, never quite still. East Asian features, warm light-tan skin, round face with full cheeks, dark eyes that close into crescents when she laughs, short straight eyebrows, a very wide grin. Black blunt bob to the chin, always a little messy, with the whole fringe dyed coral.
Always wears: an oversized plain coral retro football shirt with a cream collar and cream cuffs, worn loose; baggy light-blue denim shorts to the knee; cream socks pulled up; chunky cream trainers, scuffed, laces loose. Trip scarf loose round her neck, not knotted, both ends hanging down her front.
Who she is: says yes to everything, plans nothing, and somehow it works. Always hungry, always a little late, never worried. She moves in curves, towards food, music and animals. Big laugh with her head thrown back. Half of whatever she is eating belongs to whoever stands next to her. She knows she would miss every train without him.
Voice (locked): low, a little husky, loud, laughs in the middle of words, light non-native accent.

### The cat (working name Mango, never named on screen)
A fat ginger street cat with a cream chest and paws, a short thick tail and half-closed green eyes. It owns the town. In one shot per film it does with no effort what the two friends are struggling to do, looks at them once and walks on. It is never needed to understand the story.

### The yellow suitcase (a prop with its own reference sheet)
Shiny sunflower-yellow hard shell, rounded corners, raised ridges down the front, four black wheels, one black pull handle. About the size of a washing machine: the lid is level with Luna's elbow and Timo's hip, so she can lean an elbow on it and both can sit on it. No stickers, straps or letters. It appears on travel days only and it never goes inside a stadium.

### Locals
At most one per film, mostly their own age (a scarf seller, a fan with a drum, a waiter), drawn in the same style, in plain lilac home scarves. Always the generous one, never the joke.

### The trip scarf
Wide teal and coral blocks with a cream fringe: his colour and her colour on one scarf, a pair that belongs to no club. Both wear it clearly in the first frame of every film, and it lies under the name on the end card. It is the badge of the series.

## 5. World and look

STYLISED, not photoreal. The friends look like collectible designer art-toy figures in real miniature streetwear, in a sunny hand-built model town, filmed as if a friend holds the camera.

- Figures: adult proportions with long legs, heads only slightly larger than life, eyes smaller than a cartoon's, thick eyebrows that do the acting, simple chunky hands, hair as solid sculpted shapes. Matte soft skin with a slight handmade texture. Clothes are real fabric at toy scale (knit, felt, denim, nylon) with a visible weave. Trainers are scuffed. This is something a 23-year-old collects, not something a five-year-old watches.
- World: one invented football town on a hill. Painted houses in cream, terracotta, mint and sky blue, cobbled streets, plain cream bunting, lemon trees in pots, low walls. No letters or numbers anywhere: signs are plain colour shapes and simple pictures. The stadium is a cream bowl with four floodlight masts, seen from outside in the distance or as a bright glow. Crowds are soft shapes of colour. The match itself is never shown.
- Palette: cream base, teal for Timo, coral for Luna, sunflower yellow only for his watch and her suitcase, lilac for home fans. Shadows are warm violet. No black, no grey.
- Light: always sun. Golden late afternoon is standard, pink-gold for mornings, rain only as a sun-shower. Interiors are flooded with sun from a big window. Never night, never a dim room.
- Camera: eye level, close to faces, a small handheld wobble, one simple move per shot, soft backgrounds. Full-frame 9:16. Faces sit in the upper two thirds and the lower middle stays calm for the caption.
- Finish: one warm grade and light grain on every film. Character motion is stepped to 12 pictures per second in the edit for a stop-motion feel that hides generated wobble; this is decided once, at the look test, by showing the same clip both ways on a phone.
- One locked outfit per friend, for ever.

## 6. Music theme

One theme made for the series, about 120 beats per minute, so a beat is half a second and every cut lands on a beat. Warm afro-house with an amapiano bounce, major key. It leads with a log-drum bass and shaker and must knock on a phone speaker.

- Timo's sound: a dry tick-tock on woodblock and muted marimba, exactly on the beat, like a watch.
- Luna's sound: the loose log drum with a cowbell that lands a little late.
- The hook: a five-note "oh-oh-oh" sung by three or four young voices, rough and slightly out of tune like friends in a stand, plus three hand claps. It is used only on the payoff.
- Shape in every film: tick-tock and shaker from frame one, with no intro. The log drum comes in with the obstacle. The music dips under each spoken line. On the "No" everything drops to the tick-tock alone. On the hard cut the full groove and the "oh-oh-oh" land together. The last three claps hit the end card.
- Natural sound is as loud as the music and comes from one consistent sound set: wheels on stone, a far crowd, wind, laughter that is not cut clean.
- Never: whistling, ukulele, stomp-clap advert music, trailer drums, whoosh effects, a trending sound.

## 7. Captions

- The only caption is the line being spoken in that shot: 3 to 5 everyday words, on screen for the whole shot.
- Large bold sans-serif, sentence case, lower-middle safe area, plain white with a soft shadow, like the platform's own text.
- One text at a time. No header line, no coloured highlight word, no emoji, no word-by-word pop.
- A shot with no spoken line has no caption. If a line is cut, its caption goes with it.
- Every film is checked once with all text covered. It must still tell the story.

## 8. The shape of a film

Five to seven shots, 22 to 30 seconds, always in this order:

1. **The clash (3 to 4 seconds).** Frame one: both friends and the one big object, his way against her way.
2. **It gets worse (one or two shots).** The object makes trouble. The cat may pass here.
3. **The squeeze (3 to 4 seconds).** The clock runs out, and the idea appears as something that physically happens (the suitcase starts to roll downhill by itself).
4. **The No (3 seconds).** One of them refuses: shakes the head, shows both palms, steps back. "No. No, no, no." The music drops to the tick-tock.
5. **The cut (4 to 5 seconds).** A hard cut to both of them doing exactly that thing. A scream turns into a laugh. The full theme lands. This is the frame people screenshot.
6. **The answer (4 to 5 seconds).** Frame one again with the feeling turned round. Someone hugs the object. Both laugh, and the laugh is not cut clean.
7. **End card (1.5 seconds).**

Who says the No changes from film to film, and so does who turns out to be right.

## 9. What never happens

- Nothing that must be read: no header, sign, screen, phone, chat, ticket, document or counter. No narrator.
- No irony, no deadpan, no subtext, no joke that needs another film, no cliffhanger.
- Nobody is humiliated. The local and the fan who does not know the chant are never the target.
- No romance between the two.
- No third recurring human, no figure who appears unexplained, no more than two friends plus one local in a frame.
- No night, no dim room, no grey grade.
- No crowd in focus, no match action, no inside of the stadium beyond light, green glow and sound. The suitcase never enters a stadium.
- No object passed from hand to hand on camera: every hand-over is a cut. No precise hand work, no mirrors.
- No real club, badge, kit colour pair, stadium, city, player or brand. Never the word "soccer". No national stereotypes.
- No alcohol as the joke, no aggression, no rival fans as enemies.
- No slang of one country and no line longer than ten words.
- No logo, app, price, slogan or call to action. No talking to the camera, no selfie-vlog shots.
- No trending sound or meme format.
- No film posted without the platform's AI label.

## 10. End card

About 1.5 seconds on a plain warm cream card: the word VENUVOY in the middle, the teal-and-coral trip scarf lying flat under it like an underline, and one small line below: "See you at the next match." The last three claps of the theme land on it. No logo animation, no app, no link. The card cuts straight back to frame one, so the film loops.

## 11. Around the film (cover and post text)

- The line "When your friend packs for one night" lives on the cover image and in the post text, never inside the film.
- The post asks one question: "Plan or No Plan. Which one are you?" We never write "tag your friend"; if the characters are right, the comments do it.
- Two or three hashtags at most. The AI label is always on.
- What Venuvoy is belongs in the account name and bio, not in the films.

FIGURES: adult proportions with long legs; heads only slightly larger than life; eyes smaller than a cartoon's; thick eyebrows that do the acting; simple chunky hands; hair as solid sculpted shapes. Matte soft skin with a slight handmade texture. Clothes are real fabric at toy scale (knit, felt, denim, nylon) with a visible weave; trainers are scuffed. The suitcase is shiny hard plastic.

WORLD: one invented football town on a hill. Painted houses in cream, terracotta, mint and sky blue, cobbled streets, plain cream bunting, lemon trees in pots, low walls. A world with no letters or numbers: signs are plain colour shapes and simple pictures, and the watch has a blank face. The stadium is a cream bowl with four floodlight masts, seen only from outside, in the distance or as a bright glow. Crowds are soft colour shapes in plain lilac scarves. The match is never shown.

PALETTE: cream base; teal belongs to Timo, coral to Luna; sunflower yellow is kept for his watch and her suitcase; the trip scarf is wide teal and coral blocks with a cream fringe. Shadows are warm violet. No black and no grey.

LIGHT: always sun. Golden late afternoon is the standard, pink-gold for mornings, and rain only ever falls as a sun-shower. Interiors have a big sunny window. Never night, never a dim room.

CAMERA: a virtual 28 to 35 mm lens at eye level, close to faces, a small handheld wobble, one simple move per shot, soft backgrounds that melt into colour. Full-frame 9:16, faces in the upper two thirds, the lower middle kept calm for the caption. Frames are built on the contrast of the tall thin friend and the short friend with the wide yellow suitcase.

FINISH: one warm grade and light grain on every film. Character motion is stepped to 12 pictures per second in the edit, which reads as stop-motion and hides generated wobble; captions and the end card stay smooth. This is decided once at the look test by showing the same 4-second clip both ways on a phone. If the stepped version looks laggy or childish, the series stays at normal speed with the grade and grain only.

WARDROBE: one locked outfit per friend in every film, with no one-sided details (no single streak, no odd socks, no half tuck, no glasses), because generated pictures mirror or drop them.

WHY THIS LOOK: (1) it does not pretend that generated people are real, which is what this age group rejects, so the AI label feels natural; (2) riding a suitcase down a hill is charming in a toy world and a dangerous stunt in live action; (3) it hides the weak spots of generated video: simple hands, no text, crowds as shapes, characters that stay the same because they are strong shapes in fixed colours; (4) two colours and two heights let anyone follow who is who with the sound off; (5) it is the opposite of the first series at one glance: sun, colour and handmade warmth against night, grey and realism.

Two small motifs, one per friend. Timo is a dry tick-tock on woodblock and muted marimba, exactly on the beat, like a watch. Luna is the loose log drum with a cowbell that lands a little late. In the set-up they answer each other; on the payoff they lock together.

episodes.title: One Night
episodes.story: Timo wants to reach the match on time, but Luna's giant suitcase makes them slow all the way up the hill. At the top she sits on it, he says no, and one cut later they ride it down to the stadium, make it, and he hugs the suitcase.

episodes.title: Just In Case
episodes.story: A sun-shower catches them on the walk to the stadium; Timo pulls a rain poncho over his head from his tiny backpack, shows Luna a second one, and she looks at the ugly thing and says no. One cut later she is dancing through the rain in it and hugging his tiny backpack.

episodes.title: Try It
episodes.story: Timo wants to eat the neat sandwiches he brought from home and shakes his head at the huge, messy street flatbread Luna holds under his nose. One cut later he has a flatbread in each hand and sauce on his chin, and she is happily finishing his sandwiches.

episodes.title: No Scarf
episodes.story: Timo already has a scarf and a second one is not in the plan, so he says no to the smiling scarf seller while Luna holds one up to his face. One cut later he walks away in three scarves, a hat and a flag as a cape, prouder than anyone, and Luna has to run to keep up.

episodes.title: One Beat Late
episodes.story: Outside the gate the fans clap a rhythm: Timo knows it but claps tiny and shy, and Luna claps huge and at the wrong moment, arms down when everyone's are up. A local fan their age shows them big and slow, Timo says no, and one cut later he is clapping over his head, the loudest of all, with Luna finally in time beside him.

episodes.title: Same Face
episodes.story: Timo wants to be inside before kick-off, but at the foot of the endless stadium stairs Luna sits down with her food and says no. One cut later he is pulling her up by both hands, and on the last step they both stop dead in the green light with exactly the same open-mouthed face.

episodes.title: No Voice
episodes.story: The morning after the match they want breakfast on a sunny terrace, but neither has a voice left: mouths open, hands go to throats, nothing comes out. Luna orders eggs by flapping like a chicken, Timo shakes his head without a sound, and one cut later he is flapping too, while the waiter, who has no voice either, flaps back and points at his own scarf.

episodes.title: Wake Up, Luna
episodes.story: At sunrise Timo is dressed and wants to catch the early train, but Luna pulls the blanket over her head and says no. One cut later she walks down the sunny street wrapped in the blanket with her eyes shut, following the warm pastry he holds in front of her nose, and on the train she is wide awake eating it while he sleeps sitting bolt upright.

pilot.title: One Night
pilot.retell: His friend brought a giant suitcase that made them late for the match, so they rode it down the hill to the stadium, got there on time, and he hugged the suitcase.

shots.place: A small square outside a train station in the invented football town, late afternoon, low golden sun, long warm shadows, plain cream bunting overhead. Far away over the rooftops, four floodlight masts.
shots.seen: A yellow suitcase the size of a washing machine fills the middle of the frame. It rolls the last half metre and stops with a bump and a wobble between two friends. On the left Luna, short, in a coral football shirt, holds its handle with both hands and grins. On the right, close to the camera, Timo, tall, in a teal jacket with a tiny backpack, holds up his arm with a big yellow watch, one finger on the watch. His finger stays there. His mouth falls open and his eyes travel from the wheels up to the top of the suitcase. Both wear the same teal-and-coral scarf. Far behind them four floodlight masts stand over the roofs.
shots.heard: Timo: "Luna. It's one night!" Natural sound: suitcase wheels rattling on stone, one heavy bump, drums far away. Music: the tick-tock and shaker start on frame one.
shots.caption: Luna. It's one night!

shots.who: Luna with the suitcase; Timo's teal shoulder at the edge of the frame
shots.seen: Close on Luna beside the suitcase. Her elbow rests on the lid. She lifts her free hand flat, high above her own head, looks up at her hand, then looks at Timo and grins with all her teeth.
shots.heard: Luna: "This is the small one!" Natural sound: one hollow knock of her elbow on the lid, her short laugh.
shots.caption: This is the small one!

shots.place: A steep cobbled street going up between painted houses, same golden sun, a low wall along one side.
shots.who: Timo, Luna and the ginger cat
shots.seen: The yellow suitcase creeps uphill, hardly moving. In front Luna pulls the handle with both hands, leaning forward. Behind it, close to the camera, Timo pushes with both hands and his shoulder, his cheek pressed flat against the yellow shell, his long legs slipping on the cobbles. On the low wall beside them a fat ginger cat strolls past, overtakes them, looks back once and walks on. Timo's eyes follow the cat.
shots.heard: none (no words). Natural sound: small wheels grinding slowly on cobbles, both of them puffing, the drums a little nearer. Music: the lazy log drum comes in.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: The top of the hill. A long straight street drops away; at its end stands the stadium, a round cream bowl with four lit floodlight masts, bright in the sun, with small soft shapes of fans moving towards it.
shots.who: Timo and Luna seen from just behind, the suitcase between them
shots.seen: From just behind the two friends: the street falls away in front of them, straight down to the stadium. Timo has both hands on his head. Between them the yellow suitcase begins to roll forward by itself, away from us, down towards the stadium. Luna jumps after it and stops it with both hands flat on the lid.
shots.heard: Timo, seen from behind: "We have five minutes!" Natural sound: a far crowd and drums rising from below, the small wheels starting to rattle on their own, Luna's short gasp, a slap of two hands on plastic. Music: thins to bass and shaker.
shots.caption: We have five minutes!

shots.place: Same hilltop, camera low in front of them, the slope behind the camera.
shots.seen: Luna is already sitting on top of the suitcase, facing down the hill, feet off the ground, grinning. She pats the lid behind her twice and lifts her eyebrows at Timo. Timo, standing beside the suitcase, shakes his head, shows both palms and takes one step back.
shots.heard: Timo: "No. No, no, no." Natural sound: two pats on the lid, Luna's giggle, one squeak of a wheel. Music: drops to the tick-tock alone.
shots.caption: No. No, no, no.

shots.place: The downhill street, empty, sun flashing between the houses, bunting streaking past overhead.
shots.who: Luna and Timo, both sitting on the suitcase
shots.seen: Hard cut. Both are riding the suitcase down the street, straight towards the camera, which races backwards just ahead of them. We see them from the knees up, sitting on the yellow lid. Luna is in front with both arms in the air and her mouth wide open in a laugh, hair and scarf flying back. Timo is behind her with both hands clamped on her shoulders, eyes huge, mouth wide open in a scream. Houses and bunting streak past on both sides. Halfway through, his scream turns into a laugh and he punches one fist into the air.
shots.heard: none (no words). Natural sound: wheels roaring on cobbles, wind, Timo's long scream turning into laughter, Luna's whoop, the crowd growing louder. Music: the full groove lands with the group 'oh-oh-oh' and claps.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: The open space in front of the stadium. The entrance is a bright soft glow behind them; a few soft shapes of fans in scarves walk in. Low golden sun.
shots.seen: Framed like the first shot: Luna on the left, the yellow suitcase in the middle, Timo on the right, close. The suitcase stands still. Timo kneels beside it, out of breath, his scarf blown back over one shoulder. He looks at his watch and a huge smile spreads over his face. He throws both arms round the suitcase and presses his cheek against it with his eyes shut. Beside him Luna, bent over laughing with her hands on her knees, drops one arm across his shoulders.
shots.heard: Timo: "I love this suitcase." Natural sound: Luna's big laugh, not cut clean; the stadium roar swelling. Music: the hook runs to the last three claps.
shots.caption: I love this suitcase.

pilot.end_card: About 1.5 seconds on a plain warm cream card: the word VENUVOY in the middle, the teal-and-coral trip scarf lying flat under it like an underline, and one small line below: 'See you at the next match.' Sound: the last three claps of the theme. No logo animation, no app, no link, no slogan. The card cuts straight back to frame one (the yellow suitcase rolling in), so the film loops. Shots 28 seconds plus card: about 29.5 seconds.

production_notes: ORDER OF WORK (nothing is generated out of this order): (1) reference sheets for Timo, Luna, the suitcase and the cat: front, side, back and five expressions for each friend; the suitcase standing beside both friends for scale; one 'ride pose' still of both sitting on it. (2) LOOK GATE: one line-up still of the two friends with the suitcase, plus one 4-second speaking clip per friend, shown to the client and to three people aged 18 to 25. (3) STRIP GATE: all seven start stills side by side with no text. (4) Shot 6, then shot 7, generated first as go or no-go. (5) The other five clips. (6) A fully silent cut. (7) Voices. (8) RETELL GATE. (9) Publish with the platform's AI label on.

LOOK GATE, two questions only: 'Who is this made for?' and 'What are these two to each other?'. If anyone answers 'kids', fix the still, not the video: longer limbs, smaller eyes, more real fabric and scuffs, less toy gloss. If most answer 'a couple', first re-pose the still as mates (side by side, the suitcase between them, her fist on his arm, both laughing); if it still reads as a couple, recast Timo as a tall young woman with the same colours, watch, backpack and scripts. Nothing else in the series changes, because no script depends on gender. No film clip is generated until the client has said yes to this still.

STRIP GATE: lay the seven start stills side by side like a comic strip. A person who has read nothing must be able to tell the story from the strip alone: giant suitcase and shocked friend, slow uphill, stadium far below, she sits on it, both ride it, he hugs it. If a still does not carry its beat, the still is redesigned before any video is made.

CHECKLIST FOR EVERY START STILL: full-frame 9:16 with no band at any edge; faces in the upper two thirds and the lower middle calm for the caption; the suitcase lid level with Luna's elbow; both scarves clearly visible; nothing that looks like a letter or a number anywhere (paint it out in the still, never in the video); the watch on the same wrist as in shot 1; stadium and fans only as soft simple shapes. A still that fails is repainted. A clip that fails is rejected and generated again; it is never patched from another take.

START LATE: every still begins after the difficult action has already happened (suitcase already arriving, Luna already seated, both already riding, Timo already on his knees), so each clip only animates the easy remainder. Each clip is generated at 5 to 6 seconds and trimmed to its length in the edit. No clip is asked for more than two actions.

VOICES AND LIPS: lock one voice per friend from the 4-second test clip and run every later line through the same two voices. Only three lines need lips in sync (shots 1, 2 and 7), each on a large face with one speaker. The line in shot 4 is played from behind and the 'No' in shot 5 is carried by the head shake. The silent cut is finished and approved first; a line is added only where its clip is clean. If a line fails, it is dropped together with its caption. The film is written to work with no words at all.

SOUND AND FINISH: replace generated wheel, crowd and wind sound with one consistent set laid in the edit. Retime the bump in shot 1, the pats in shot 5 and the cut into shot 6 onto the beat. One warm grade and light grain over all clips; the 12-pictures-per-second step is applied only if it passed the look test. Check the top and bottom edge of every clip for bands before it enters the edit.

SHOT 1. Start picture: the suitcase already large in the middle of the frame, half a metre from its stop, Luna's two hands on the handle; Timo close on the right with his watch arm up and one finger on the watch, already looking at the suitcase; floodlight masts soft over the roofs; both scarves clear. What moves: the suitcase rolls the last bit, bumps and wobbles; Timo's eyes climb it and his mouth opens; he speaks. Plan B: if the suitcase bends while rolling, start with it already parked and only wobbling. If the lips are wrong, keep the picture and drop the line and caption; the open mouth already says it.

SHOT 2. Start picture: Luna close, elbow already on the lid, grinning, Timo's shoulder at the edge. What moves: only her free arm goes up and her eyes follow it; she speaks. Plan B: if the raised hand deforms, she pats the lid twice with a flat hand instead. If the line fails, use 2 seconds of the proud grin with no caption and give the spare second to shot 3.

SHOT 3. Start picture: side view, the street rising from left to right; Timo's cheek already flat on the yellow shell, close to the camera; Luna ahead, pulling; the cat already on the wall one step behind them. What moves: the suitcase creeps a hand's width, feet slip, the cat walks through the frame and looks back. Plan B: if the cat or the figures drift, make the shot without the cat (Timo lifts his head and looks at his watch) and let the cat first appear in film 2. If the wheels melt into the cobbles, crop tighter so the wheels are out of frame.

SHOT 4. Start picture: from behind at shoulder height; Timo's hands already on his head; the suitcase between them already a hand's width ahead, starting to roll; the stadium clear and simple at the end of the street (cream bowl, four lit masts, bigger than a blur) with soft colour shapes of fans near it. What moves: the suitcase rolls about a metre away from us; Luna steps after it and lands both flat hands on the lid. Timo's line is recorded separately and laid in; no lips are seen. Plan B: start with Luna already holding the suitcase back by the handle, leaning back with her heels skidding, while it pulls downhill like a dog on a lead. If the stadium grows letters or sharp people, repaint the still before animating.

SHOT 5. Start picture: low front angle; Luna already seated on the lid, grinning; Timo beside the suitcase with both palms already up. What moves: two pats on the lid behind her; his head shakes; one step back. The 'No' is laid in as sound, and the shaking head hides any lip mismatch. Plan B: frame over Timo's shoulder so we see only his shaking head and palms from behind, and Luna's face carries the shot.

SHOT 6, GENERATED FIRST. Start picture: the approved ride-pose still: knees up, both already seated and already moving, hair and scarves blown back, background already streaked, the yellow lid visible under them, wheels out of frame. What moves: the background streams past, small bounces, her arms stay up, his scream turns into a laugh, one fist goes up. Never show getting on, the wheels or the stop. Plan B1: a chest-up two-shot of the two faces in the wind, cut in two pieces at the moment the scream becomes a laugh. Plan B2, only if no take is clean: Luna rides alone with her arms up and Timo runs behind pushing, screaming and then laughing; the story holds. If none of these comes out clean, stop before spending on the other shots.

SHOT 7, GENERATED SECOND. Start picture: the same framing as shot 1; the suitcase standing still in the middle; Timo already on his knees with one arm on it, looking at his watch; Luna already bent over laughing; the entrance as a bright glow with soft shapes. What moves: his smile, the line, both arms round the suitcase, cheek down, eyes shut; her arm drops across his shoulders. He says the line before his cheek touches the suitcase, so the mouth is clear. Plan B: a silent hug with Luna's laugh and no caption; the picture alone answers shot 1. If her arm on his shoulders deforms, she stays bent over laughing with no contact.
END CARD: built in the edit with real type, never generated. The scarf under the name is one designed still. It lasts about 1.5 seconds and holds no moving picture behind the text.

RETELL GATE: show the finished film once, muted, on a phone, to a young viewer and to an adult with English as a second language who have seen nothing (and to the AI test viewer). Ask only 'What happened?'. Release the film only if the answer matches: 'His friend brought a giant suitcase that made them late for the match, so they rode it down the hill, got there on time, and he hugged the suitcase.' Then repeat once with all captions covered.

SMALL QUESTIONS WE ACCEPT: viewers asked how the two stop, why the street is empty and what happens to the suitcase at the gate. The stop stays behind the cut (showing it adds a hard clip and a shot), the street stays empty so the ride reads cleanly, and the suitcase never goes inside: the film ends outside, and the bible keeps it out of every stadium. None of these three stopped any viewer from understanding the story.
decisions: WINNER: 'Plan, No Plan' (the duo), taken as the base. Its pilot was understood best by the cold viewers (10, 9 and 9 out of 10; all three said they would follow), it has the highest judge average (7.25), it is first for making without faults and second for clarity, vibe and client. The client's two hardest complaints were 'I understood nothing' and 'no screw-ups', and this concept answers both best. Title and names (Timo, Luna) are kept.

TWO LEADS, NOT THREE. In all four pilots with a third friend, viewers asked 'who is she?' or 'who is he?', and all three viewers named 'only two people' as the reason the duo was clear. I did not take the trio from 'Away Crew' even though the client and vibe judges ranked that concept first: its pilot was understood less well (8.67), had no physical high point, and carried rain, a lid opening and a second costume.

'TWO IS NOT A CREW' AND THE COUPLE RISK are answered inside two people: friends-not-couple rules in the tone (the big hug goes to the object, no hand-holding, mates' body language), a local their own age in most films, the cat, and the cover line 'When your friend packs for one night'. This risk is not proven away: it is tested at the look gate with the question 'What are these two to each other?', with a concrete plan B (re-pose, then recast Timo as a woman) before any video is made.

NO HEADER LINE (from 'Away Crew', backed by the vibe and client judges). The 'When your friend...' line moves to the cover and post text. This also removes the clash one viewer saw between a header about overpacking and a film about being late: the film is now one idea, the suitcase is the problem and then the answer.

CAPTION DISCIPLINE from 'Away Crew': the only text is the current spoken line, 3 to 5 words, one at a time, held for the whole shot, no coloured words. Five short captions, 21 words in total, none needed to follow the story.

THE WATCH AS THE CLOCK is kept from the duo and made a series rule (finger on watch, hands on head, look and smile). The plot line 'The match starts in five minutes!' became the more natural 'We have five minutes!', spoken from behind so no lips are needed.

THE REFUSAL AND THE HARD CUT ('No. No, no, no.' then the opposite) is made the signature of every film, as the vibe judge asked. Who refuses and who is right rotate, so neither friend becomes the fool: Luna is right in three films, Timo in three, both in two.

PILOT SHOT 4 REBUILT on the make judge's idea: the idea no longer depends on a small look at the wheels; the suitcase visibly starts to roll downhill by itself and Luna catches it. The stadium is drawn larger and clearer because one viewer only understood it through the caption.

PILOT SHOT 3 CHANGED: the stairs became a cobbled slope (stairs and walking backwards generate badly), and Timo now pushes with his cheek on the suitcase instead of standing at the top tapping his watch, because a viewer found him annoying for not helping.

KEPT 'This is the small one!' although the clarity judge wants no joke that lives only in a line: it was called the funniest line of all five pilots, and the series needs quotable lines to feel like friends. It is now doubled by a gesture (her hand held high above her own head), and the film loses nothing if the line is cut.

DESIGNS STRIPPED of one-sided details on the make judge's advice: no glasses, a whole coral fringe instead of one streak, matching socks, no half tuck, a scarf of wide blocks, the watch worn over the cuff with no wrist named in any script. Timo's zipped track top is kept as football terrace style so he is neat, not uncool.

THE SUITCASE RESIZED to washing-machine size (lid at Luna's elbow) so two people can plausibly sit on it, and the ride is filmed from the knees up with the wheels out of frame. The ride clip is generated first as the go or no-go, then the closing shot (the 'closing clip first' rule from 'Away Crew').

LOOK: the phrase and direction from 'Away Crew': collectible art-toy figures in streetwear with adult proportions, not clay puppets, plus its world without letters. The trip scarf as the badge of the series (worn clearly in frame one, lying under the name on the end card) is the client judge's steal, in the duo's own teal and coral.

FROM 'Trip Trip Hooray': the rule that every sound that matters has a picture, the muted retell gate before release, the silent-cut-first working method, and the street cat for one shot per film. Rejected: a fully wordless series (the judges said mute puppets read as mascots or children's television with nothing to quote) and the umbrella that shoots out of the suitcase (cartoon magic that viewers could not explain).

FROM 'First Away': the comic-strip gate of start stills, the 12-pictures-per-second finish (as a tested option, not a certainty, because the vibe judge warned it can read as children's television), and the season's emotional image of the pitch opening at the top of the stairs, turned into the film 'Same Face'. Rejected: the 'Mission 1' header, four characters, the station and train doors, and the illogical 'too heavy, so add a person' fix.

FROM 'Match Day Diary': nothing structural. The selfie format and the selfie last frame are rejected: an arm at the lens and a wide lens distort faces, three camera modes made viewers ask who is filming, and the pilot must end on the hug with nothing added after it.

FROM 'Away Crew' films: 'No Voice' (called the best episode idea in the pack) and every hand-over written as a cut. Rejected: Kofi's line 'You never know', because it promises that the suitcase will be opened and viewers of another pilot felt cheated when it was not; and the poncho pilot. The poncho idea survives as film 2, where Timo's plan is the hero.

EPISODES: dropped 'Left or Right' (it cross-cuts two places and splits the two friends, which breaks the clearest thing about the series). 'The Chant' moved out of the stand to a wall outside the gate and is told with arms up and arms down, not with sound. No film hangs on a roar alone. The stadium stays light, glow and sound in every film.

MUSIC: the duo's two motifs are kept, but led by the log drum, with a few rough voices and the hook only on the payoff, to stay away from stomp-clap advert music as the vibe judge warned. The tempo is set to 120 so cuts fall on half-second beats.

END CARD: plain card, 1.5 seconds, no picture moving behind the text. Every viewer asked what VENUVOY is; the brief allows the brand only to sign, so the film does not explain it. The line 'See you at the next match' says football, and the account name and bio say the rest.

NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN GENERATED OR TESTED YET. The look, the couple question, the ride clip and the muted retell are gates with a stated plan B, not results. Only one suitcase film is made, so the viewers' warning about five versions of the same joke and reused names does not apply.
